reasons.reader_question: Sharp closing dilemma: rubbing to the queen alone, or keep faith with Kiran and the shared-map principle. The carving's last word stays open.
reasons.change: Oath broken in public, commission and crown roll lost, Neshar wins self-rule, and Rohan learns the truth about Harish. Power and knowledge both shift.
reasons.romance_movement: There is a new reason to trust: no rope can verify them now. The fold test, Dhanu's Rest and the public palm show faith kept without proof.
reasons.shown_chemistry: Responsive acts carry it: lurching when she lurches, the hand beside hers not touching, his glance at the laid gloves. Quiet but earned.
reasons.character_logic: Ila is sound. Sarala grants all four demands at once on a muddled 'already paid' rationale. Ila waiting thirteen days to tell Rohan goes unexplained.
reasons.stakes_and_cost: The commission is a real, chosen price paid on the page. The final choice costs a loyalty either way.
reasons.prose: Clean, concrete and low on AI tells. Some references are opaque, the 'tooth' image echoes, and consecutive paragraphs open with 'She' and 'He'.
reasons.continuity: Ages, day counts (35, 56), toes, pace, twelve years, sixty-one winters and the Kiran request all match canon. Rohan's rope end is on the table, not in his hands; minor beat drift.

fixes: At '"Granted," said Sarala. "All four."' the concession is too cheap and its logic muddled (Irrational behaviour). Tie it to her want to keep the kingdom whole past her death: a valley everyone can see is one Pritam cannot buy. Add one condition or cost she sets, such as the council seat's first duty being Pritam's recapture, so the grant is bargained, not handed over.

At 'Whichever way she moved, she would be breaking faith' the Kunal side of the dilemma is only implied. Add one line making it explicit: a private first reading is crown exclusivity again, the thing she broke her oath to end an hour ago. Then the reader feels both loyalties pulling, not just Kiran's.

Clarify opaque references: 'where the mountain had once taken the path away' (name the twice-rope rule plainly), 'beside the crown's word' (the Ladder has no crown name; say her survey label), and 'when he put out the lamp' (anchor it or cut it). Also split the consecutive 'She took off her gloves'/'She laid them' and 'She dipped'/'She laid the sheets' openings.
reader_question: Will Ila hand the unread rubbing to the queen alone, breaking faith with Kiran and Kunal, and what does the carving's last word say?
new_facts_assessment: Both draft facts are needed and consistent. Their IDs collide with existing continuity F618 ('three weeks and a day', which conflicts with the chapter) and F622/F623 duplicates; renumber and retire the stale ones. Several facts are unlisted: Kunal signing left-handed, Ila's oath wording, twelve years since the brass rule, Ila's promise to Kiran, and the 'put out the lamp' moment. Log them or cut them.
